items.title: ⚠️ Deadline for Mass Regularization Ends as Supreme Court Threatens Suspension
items.body: Over 1 million applications were submitted by the June 30 deadline for Spain's extraordinary regularization of migrants, far exceeding the government's initial estimate of 750,000. However, the Supreme Court has raised concerns that the process may violate EU migration law and is considering referring the case to the Court of Justice of the European Union, potentially suspending the entire program. The court gave the involved parties five days to present arguments. The regularization, which grants legal status to undocumented residents, has been in effect since April 14, but applications could face uncertainty if the suspension proceeds.

items.title: Spain Faces Austria in World Cup Round of 32 on July 2
items.body: Spain, which finished first in its group undefeated, will play Austria in the round of 32 at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The match is scheduled for July 2 at 21:00 Spanish peninsular time and will take place in Guadalajara, Mexico. The national team is aiming for its second World Cup title.

items.title: Government to Raise VAT on Tourist Apartments to 21% in New Housing Package
items.body: The Spanish government plans to approve a housing package in July via royal decree that includes raising VAT on tourist apartments to 21%. The package, negotiated between PSOE and Sumar, also includes measures to stabilize rental prices and crack down on rental fraud. The VAT increase directly targets the short-term rental market, a sector popular with property investors and tourists.

items.title: Supreme Court Judge Questions Validity of Rental Contract Extensions
items.body: A Supreme Court judge has expressed doubts about the legality of extraordinary rental contract extensions that affect up to 1 million tenants. The extensions, which cover contracts expiring between April 30 and December 31, could be invalidated, leaving renters without the right to renew. The government has announced it will introduce a new housing package that includes fresh extension measures, but legal uncertainty remains for many households.

items.title: Euribor Holds at 2.80%, but Variable Mortgages Cost Up to €1,500 More a Year
items.body: The Euribor closed June at 2.80%, and while it has stabilized, holders of variable-rate mortgages still face annual repayment increases of up to €1,500 compared to last year. The European Central Bank's next meeting is on July 23, with rates expected to remain between 2.6% and 2.9% until then. Homeowners with variable loans will continue to feel the pinch throughout the summer.

items.title: ECB's Lagarde Signals Limited Further Rate Hikes Despite Iran Conflict
items.body: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde indicated that future interest rate increases will be moderate, even as the conflict in Iran pushes up inflation. The ECB raised rates by 0.25 points in June, and May inflation stood at 3.2%. Lagarde said the European economy is more resilient than during the 2022-2023 Ukraine crisis, suggesting that borrowing costs may not surge dramatically.

items.title: Number of Foreign Self-Employed Workers in Spain Reaches All-Time High
items.body: Spain registered a record 519,137 foreign autónomos (self-employed workers) in May 2026, a 7.25% increase from a year earlier and a 119% jump since 2008. The total number of self-employed in the country is 3.46 million. The surge reflects the growing role of foreign entrepreneurs and is expected to accelerate with the ongoing regularization process.

items.title: Law of Grandchildren Sparks Political Row as PP Accuses Government of Vote Grab
items.body: The Law of Grandchildren, which allows descendants of Civil War exiles to obtain Spanish nationality, has drawn fierce criticism from the Partido Popular, which calls it "electoral engineering." Official figures show 2.4 million appointment requests and over 544,000 approved nationalities since the law took effect. The government defends the measure as reparative justice, but the controversy could lead to political challenges.

items.title: Spain to Scrap Electricity Tax, Cutting Household Bills by 6%
items.body: The government will phase out the electricity production tax (IVPEE) by 2028, reducing it to 5% in 2026 and 3.5% in 2027 before full elimination. The move is expected to lower typical household electricity bills by up to 6%, though it will cost the state about €2.7 billion in lost revenue over two years.

items.title: Tax Agency Raids 41 Real Estate Firms in Fraud Probe Across Six Regions
items.body: Spain's Tax Agency launched Operation Insulae, deploying 170 officials to inspect 41 real estate businesses in six autonomous communities for suspected tax fraud. Investigators are looking into unreported cash payments and illegal commissions in Valencia, Andalusia, Catalonia, Madrid, the Canary Islands, and the Balearic Islands. A total of 49 companies and 18 individuals are under investigation.

items.title: Coastal Summer Rentals Hit Record Highs, Topping €1,100 a Week
items.body: The average weekly rent for a summer coastal property in Spain has surged 17.5% year-on-year to a record €1,142. The Balearic Islands are the most expensive at €2,923 per week, while the Costa del Sol saw a 23.3% jump. No coastal area registered a price drop, putting vacation rentals out of reach for many.

items.title: US Supreme Court Rejects Spain's Appeal, Clearing Way for Renewable Energy Awards
items.body: The US Supreme Court denied Spain's request for legal protection, finalizing a DC Circuit Court ruling that allows the enforcement of international arbitration awards against Spain. These awards stem from Madrid's retroactive cuts to renewable energy subsidies, which hit foreign investors. The decision opens the door for claimants to collect millions of euros.

items.title: Spain's Youth Are Worse Off Than Three Decades Ago, Report Finds
items.body: Young people in Spain are in a worse social and economic position than they were in 1995, according to a new synthetic indicator from Fundación PwC. The index, which tracks 39 variables covering demographics, employment, education, and housing, shows conditions have steadily deteriorated since the 2008 financial crisis and have never recovered to pre-crisis levels.

items.title: Congress Votes to Keep Public Health System Drug Prices Confidential
items.body: Spain's Congress approved an amendment making the prices of medications in the public health system secret. The measure was tacked onto a newborn screening bill and has been criticized by Podemos for reducing transparency. The direct impact on patients' access to medicines remains unclear.
